places.summary: Red sandstone castle that was the Moorish capital of the Algarve, above a hillside town and a Gothic cathedral. The best-preserved castle in the region.
facts: Ticket ~€3
Combine with Silves Cathedral next door
Medieval fair in August
places.kids: Kids love walking the red sandstone battlements of this real Moorish castle; it's compact, so the visit is perfect for little legs.
places.caution: Wall walks have low parapets in places.

places.name: Monchique & Fóia
places.summary: Fóia is the Algarve's highest point (902 m), with views to the coast on clear days; Monchique below is a hill town of cork and chestnut woods. Cooler and greener than the coast.
facts: Drive to the summit; free
Try medronho liqueur in Monchique
Hike options around Picota
places.season: Often in cloud in winter; clearest in the morning.
places.caution: Wildfire risk in summer; check warnings.
places.kids: Kids enjoy the drive up to the highest point in the Algarve and the view to the sea; it is cooler up top, so bring a layer.

places.name: Ria Formosa islands (Culatra / Deserta)
places.summary: Lagoon nature park of channels, salt marshes and barrier islands with car-free fishing village Culatra and the empty beaches of Ilha Deserta. Good for birdwatching (flamingos, spoonbills).
facts: Public ferries from Olhão to Culatra/Armona; boats from Faro to Deserta
Check last-boat-back times
Bring water and shade
places.season: Reduced ferry timetables in winter.
places.kids: Kids love the ferry ride and the wide, gentle lagoon-side beaches with no cars; pick the Culatra ferry for a short trip, and take shade, water and snacks.

places.name: Ilha de Tavira
places.summary: Long sandy barrier island with calm, warmer water than the western Algarve. Reached by short ferry or water taxi.
facts: Ferry from Quatro Águas runs year-round, small fare
Some cafés near the landing; quiet further along
Walk to Praia do Barril (anchor cemetery)
places.season: Ferry less frequent in winter.
places.kids: Kids enjoy the short ferry ride and the long sandy beach with warm, gentle water; a boardwalk leads from the pier to the beach and cafés.

places.name: Cacela Velha
places.summary: Tiny whitewashed village with a fort and church on a bluff above the Ria Formosa lagoon. At low tide you can wade across to the beach.
facts: Small car park fills in summer
Check tide times to cross to the beach
Great at sunset
places.kids: Kids love paddling across the lagoon to the sandbar beach at low tide; check tide times, since at high tide you need the little boat.

places.name: Alvor Boardwalk
places.summary: Wooden boardwalk loop through the dunes and estuary between Alvor village and the beach. Easy, flat walk with birdlife.
facts: Free; about 1–1.5 hours for the loop
Park in Alvor village
Good with children
places.kids: Kids enjoy spotting crabs and wading birds from the long, flat wooden boardwalk; it's ideal for buggies and bikes, but has no shade.

places.name: Castro Marim
places.summary: Border town with a castle and fort overlooking the Guadiana and salt marshes of a nature reserve with flamingos. Next to Spain.
facts: Castle ticket ~€2
Flamingos in the salt pans of the nature reserve
Medieval festival in late summer
places.kids: Kids love exploring the castle and fort, especially during the Medieval Days festival; also look for flamingos in the salt pans nearby.

places.name: Faro Old Town & Cathedral
places.summary: Walled Cidade Velha entered through the Arco da Vila, with storks nesting on rooftops and a cathedral whose tower looks over the lagoon. Nearby Igreja do Carmo has a bone chapel.
facts: Cathedral with tower climb ~€5
Bone chapel at Igreja do Carmo ~€2
Allow 1.5 hours
places.kids: Kids enjoy climbing the cathedral tower and spotting storks' nests on the old town walls; finish at the marina by the Ciência Viva centre.

places.name: Funchal Old Town (Zona Velha)
places.summary: The old fishermen's quarter around Rua de Santa Maria, known for its painted-door art project, small restaurants and bars. Ends at the yellow São Tiago Fort by the sea.
facts: Free to wander
Best in late afternoon and evening for dinner
Lower station of the Monte cable car is at its edge
Touts from restaurants can be insistent
places.kids: Kids love spotting the painted doors of Rua de Santa Maria and watching the boats by the fort; combine it with the cable car up to Monte, which starts right here.
places.facilities: Cafés, public toilets near the cable car station

places.name: Mercado dos Lavradores
places.summary: Funchal's 1940s Art Deco market hall with azulejo panels, piled with exotic fruit, flowers and a fish hall selling black scabbardfish. Busiest on Friday and Saturday mornings.
facts: Free entry
Fruit sellers offer tastings then charge tourist prices — ask the price per kg first
Come in the morning, especially Fri/Sat
Fish hall is best before noon
places.kids: Kids love the piles of strange tropical fruit and the huge black scabbard fish downstairs; go on a weekday morning and ask stall-holders for a taste before buying, as samples get pricey.

places.name: Monte cable car & toboggan
places.summary: Ride the cable car from the old town up to the hill village of Monte, visit the church of Nossa Senhora do Monte, then slide back down the steep streets in a wicker toboggan steered by two carreiros in straw hats.
facts: Cable car one way ~€13, return ~€19
Toboggan ~€30–35 per sledge for two, runs to Livramento (not all the way down); taxi or walk from there
Can combine with Monte Palace Garden next door
Queues for the toboggan at midday on cruise-ship days
places.caution: The toboggan runs on public road; keep hands and feet inside.
places.kids: Kids love the cable-car ride over the rooftops and the wicker toboggan slide down the steep street; little ones sit on a parent's lap, and go early to beat cruise-ship queues.

places.name: Monte Palace Tropical Garden
places.summary: A huge hillside garden in Monte with oriental gardens, koi ponds, azulejo panels, cycads and a mineral and African art museum. One of the best gardens in Portugal.
facts: ~€15 adult
Allow 2 hours; lots of steps
Next to the Monte cable car top station
Quieter at opening time
places.kids: Kids love the giant koi carp, the swans and the little bridges and waterfalls; it is very steep with many steps, so use a carrier for toddlers and save legs for the way back up.

places.name: Madeira Botanical Garden
places.summary: Terraced botanical garden above Funchal with famous geometric flower beds, succulents and native Madeiran plants, plus wide views over the bay.
facts: ~€6 adult
Linked to Monte by a second cable car (Teleférico do Jardim Botânico)
Bus or taxi from Funchal centre (~15 min)
Small natural history museum included
places.kids: Kids love the parrots and macaws in the bird park (Loiro Parque) and the cactus beds; bring snacks and a hat, as the terraces are sunny and stepped.

places.name: Whale & dolphin watching from Funchal
places.summary: Boat trips from Funchal marina to see resident dolphins, pilot whales and, seasonally, sperm and Bryde's whales. Sightings rate is high year-round.
facts: ~€50–65 adult for a 2.5–3 h trip
Book a day or two ahead; morning trips usually calmer
Choose operators with sighting guarantees
Take seasickness tablets if prone
places.season: Trips can be cancelled in rough seas, more often in winter.
places.kids: Kids love seeing dolphins leap beside the boat, which happens on most trips; choose a bigger catamaran for small children and sit at the back to avoid seasickness.
places.caution: Small fast RIB boats are bumpy and often have a minimum age of about 6–8; take a catamaran with younger kids.

places.name: Cabo Girão skywalk
places.summary: One of Europe's highest sea cliffs (about 580 m), with a glass-floored skywalk hanging over the drop and views of terraced fields far below and Funchal to the east.
facts: Small entrance fee (~€2)
Free parking, fills mid-morning on cruise days
Best early or late for fewer tour buses
Combine with Câmara de Lobos
places.caution: Low cloud can hide the view completely; check the webcam before driving up.
places.kids: Kids love standing on the glass floor 580 m above the sea; it is a short flat walk from the car park, so it works even with a buggy.

places.name: Câmara de Lobos
places.summary: Fishing town just west of Funchal with brightly painted boats pulled up in a tiny harbour, the viewpoint Churchill painted, and bars serving poncha.
facts: Free; easy bus or 15 min drive from Funchal
Try poncha (rum, honey, lemon) in a local bar
Pico da Torre viewpoint above town
Good at sunset
places.kids: Kids love the brightly painted fishing boats pulled up on the pebbles and the harbour cats; walk the seafront promenade and have an ice cream by the bay.

places.name: Pico do Arieiro
places.summary: Madeira's third-highest peak (1,818 m), reachable by car, with jagged volcanic ridges and often a sea of clouds below. The start of the classic PR1 ridge trail to Pico Ruivo.
facts: Free; parking at the summit, gets full for sunrise
Sunrise is spectacular — arrive 30–45 min before
Bring warm layers: can be near 0 °C at dawn
About 40 min drive from Funchal
places.caution: Do not let kids start down the PR1 ridge trail, which has sheer drops and tunnels.
places.kids: Kids love being above the clouds and spotting the radar dome; stay on the short paved path near the summit café and bring warm layers, as it can be near freezing at dawn.

places.name: Achada do Teixeira (short route to Pico Ruivo)
places.summary: Car park and trailhead above Santana from which a paved path (PR1.2) climbs gently to Pico Ruivo summit in about an hour. The easiest way to reach Madeira's highest point.
facts: About 2.8 km each way, 2–2.5 h return
Free parking at the end of the road from Santana
Small mountain hut near the summit sells drinks
Basalt 'Homem em Pé' rock formation by the car park
places.caution: Steady climb with steep drops beside parts of the path; hold younger children's hands.
places.kids: Kids love reaching Madeira's highest peak on the easiest route (about 1h15 each way on a paved path with steps); go in the morning for clear views and take water and layers.

places.name: Porto Moniz natural pools
places.summary: Natural swimming pools formed in black volcanic rock, refilled by Atlantic waves crashing over the edge. The managed complex has lifeguards, changing rooms and sunbeds.
facts: ~€3 adult
Free wild pools nearby too
Bring water shoes; rock is sharp
Opening hours shorter in winter
places.season: Best May–October; the pools stay open year-round but can close when the sea is very rough.
places.kids: Kids love swimming in the volcanic rock pools while waves crash over the outer wall; the complex has lifeguards in season and a shallow children's pool, so it is the safest sea swim in Madeira.
places.facilities: Changing rooms, lockers, café, lifeguards in season

places.name: Seixal black sand beach
places.summary: Small beach of black volcanic sand framed by green cliffs and waterfalls, one of the most photogenic spots on the north coast. Seixal also has natural rock pools.
facts: Free; small car park
Showers and a beach bar in summer
Combine with Porto Moniz
Water entry is steep with waves
places.caution: Waves can be strong and the beach shelves quickly; keep little ones at the water's edge.
places.kids: Kids love the black volcanic sand and the waterfall-streaked green cliffs behind; swim only on calm days and stay near the shore.

places.name: Fanal forest
places.summary: Upland meadow at about 1,100 m dotted with gnarled centuries-old laurel (til) trees, often wrapped in drifting fog. Short, easy walking and very atmospheric.
facts: Free; roadside parking off the ER209
Fog makes the best photos — go in the morning
Cows graze freely
About 25 min uphill from Porto Moniz
places.season: Can be cold and wet; fog almost guaranteed outside summer.
places.kids: Kids love the twisted ancient laurel trees and the cows wandering through the mist, like a fairy-tale forest; wander the open meadows rather than a set trail and bring jackets.

places.name: Whale watching from Ponta Delgada
places.summary: Boat trips (RIB or catamaran) guided by lookouts on shore, with very high chances of dolphins and good chances of sperm whales year-round; blue and fin whales pass in spring.
facts: ~€60–70 adult for about 3 h
Book ahead; trips are cancelled in rough seas
RIBs are faster but wetter; catamarans better for kids
Morning trips usually calmer
places.season: Spring (Apr–May) is best for baleen whales; winter trips are often cancelled for weather.
places.kids: Kids love seeing dolphins (almost always) and often whales; choose a catamaran-type boat with younger children and take seasickness tablets beforehand.
places.caution: Many companies set a minimum age around 5–6 for RIB zodiac trips.

places.name: Sete Cidades & Vista do Rei
places.summary: A huge volcanic caldera holding the twin Blue and Green lakes, seen best from the Vista do Rei viewpoint on the rim. Below, the village of Sete Cidades sits on the lake shore.
facts: Free; parking at Vista do Rei
Also see Boca do Inferno viewpoint (short walk) and Lagoa do Canário
Rim walk along the caldera is a fine half-day hike
Check webcams (SpotAzores) — it is often in cloud
places.caution: Cloud often fills the crater; come back later in the day if it is fogged in.
places.kids: Kids love the twin lakes, one blue and one green, and the legend about them; drive down to the village to walk the flat lakeside and the bridge between the lakes.

places.name: Ponta da Ferraria thermal pool
places.summary: A natural ocean pool in a lava cove where hot spring water mixes with the Atlantic, with ropes to hold on to. Best around low tide when the water is warmest.
facts: Sea pool is free; a spa building next door is ticketed
Go at low tide — check a tide table
Steep road down; parking at the end
Water shoes help
places.caution: Waves can surge into the pool; only go on calm days and keep younger kids out.
places.kids: Kids love bathing in warm sea water heated by a volcanic spring; go at low tide when the water is warmest and hold the ropes.
places.season: Best in calm summer weather.

places.name: Caldeira Velha
places.summary: Small nature park in a fern-filled ravine with a warm iron-rich waterfall pool and hotter thermal pools. Feels like a jungle.
facts: ~€10 to bathe, less for a visit only
Time slots; book ahead in summer
Changing rooms on site
Iron-rich water stains light swimwear
places.kids: Kids love the warm waterfall pool in a jungle of giant ferns; bring old dark swimwear (the iron-rich water stains) and book a time slot in summer.

places.name: Gorreana Tea Plantation
places.summary: Europe's oldest continuously operating tea plantation, founded in 1883, on the north coast. You can see the old machinery at work, taste free tea and walk among the bushes.
facts: Free entry and tasting
Short walking trails through the plantation
Shop sells local black and green tea
Porto Formoso plantation is nearby too
places.kids: Kids love the rows of tea bushes and watching the old machines roll and dry leaves; tasting is free, so try it with a short walk among the bushes.

places.name: Furnas Lake & caldeiras
places.summary: Crater lake whose north shore steams with fumaroles where pots of cozido are buried in the ground to cook for about six hours. Watch them being lifted out around noon.
facts: Small parking/entry fee to the fumarole area
Cozido pots come out about 12:00–13:00
Walking path around the lake (~9 km)
Gruta do Padre José Jacinto chapel on the shore
places.kids: Kids love watching cozido stew pots being pulled out of the hot ground around midday; the flat lakeside path is good for buggies and scooters.

places.name: Terra Nostra Garden
places.summary: 18th-century botanical garden in Furnas with an enormous yellow-brown iron-rich thermal pool at about 35–40 °C, plus camellias, ferns and cycads.
facts: ~€10–15 adult; bathing included
Wear an old dark swimsuit — water stains
Showers and changing rooms; pool busy at midday
Evening hours in summer
places.kids: Kids love swimming in the big warm orange thermal pool and exploring paths among giant ferns; bring dark swimwear and a towel, as the iron water stains.

places.name: Poça da Dona Beija
places.summary: Set of small, lantern-lit thermal pools beside a stream in Furnas, open late into the evening. Great after a day of sightseeing.
facts: ~€8 adult
Lockers and showers
Open into the late evening
Queues at peak times
places.kids: Kids love the warm small pools lit up in the evening; book a time slot in busy periods and bring dark swimwear.

places.name: Salto do Prego waterfall hike
places.summary: Loop trail from the village of Faial da Terra through a lush valley to a 20 m waterfall, passing the restored hamlet of Sanguinho.
facts: About 4.5 km loop, 2 h
Free; parking in Faial da Terra
Moderate with some steep, slippery stretches
Swimming possible in the pool below the fall
places.season: Waterfall strongest after autumn/winter rain.
places.kids: Kids love the tall waterfall and the abandoned stone village of Sanguinho on the way; it is about 2–3 hours return on a muddy track, so wear proper shoes.

places.name: Monte Brasil
places.summary: Volcanic peninsula beside Angra wrapped by the walls of the São João Baptista fortress, with forest trails and viewpoints over the town and bay.
facts: Free; trails start from the fortress or park
Loop around 7 km, about 2 h
Pico das Cruzinhas viewpoint by car
places.kids: Kids love the cannons in the fort and the picnic and playground area with deer enclosure near the top; drive up to the picnic park and take the short walk to the viewpoints.

places.name: Algar do Carvão
places.summary: A rare open lava tube: you descend into the empty throat of an extinct volcano, past mossy walls and stalactites of silica, to a clear rain-fed lake at the bottom.
facts: ~€10 adult; combined ticket with Gruta do Natal available
Limited opening outside summer — check before going
Steep steps, can be wet
Bring a jacket: cool and damp inside
places.season: Opening days and hours are reduced from autumn to spring.
places.kids: Kids love climbing into a real volcano chimney to the green lake at the bottom; it is damp with many steps, so bring a jacket and good shoes.

places.name: Biscoitos natural pools
places.summary: Swimming pools in black lava rock on Terceira's north coast, with ladders and sunbathing terraces. The village also has a small wine museum and vineyards in lava-stone pens.
facts: Free; changing rooms in summer
Biscoitos wine museum nearby
Best on calm, sunny days
places.season: Best June–September.
places.kids: Kids love swimming in the black lava rock pools with ladders and walkways; go on a calm summer day and keep younger children in the inner pools.

places.name: Capelinhos Volcano
places.summary: Moonscape of ash and cinder left by the 1957–58 eruption that added land to Faial's western tip, with a half-buried lighthouse and an excellent underground interpretation centre.
facts: Interpretation centre ~€10; lighthouse climb included
Walk up the ash cone for views
About 30 min from Horta
Windy and exposed
places.caution: Stay on paths; ash slopes are loose and cliffs unstable.
places.kids: Kids love the moon-like landscape of the 1957 eruption and the underground visitor centre with its film; the centre is good on rainy days.

places.name: Lisbon Zoo
places.summary: A large, long-established zoo in the city with around 2,000 animals, from elephants and giraffes to big cats. It has a dolphin and sea-lion show, a cable car over the park and plenty of shade.
facts: Adults ~€30, children 3–12 ~€21, under 3 free
Next to Jardim Zoológico metro station (blue line)
The cable car (teleférico) over the park is included and kids love it
Check the dolphin and sea-lion presentation times at the entrance
places.kids: Kids love the dolphin show, the cable-car ride over the enclosures and the reptile house; arrive at opening and check presentation times first.

places.name: Pavilhão do Conhecimento (Ciência Viva)
places.summary: Lisbon's hands-on science centre in Parque das Nações, run by Ciência Viva. Interactive exhibitions let children experiment with physics, light and sound, with a dedicated area for the youngest.
facts: Closed Mondays
Right next to the Oceanário: easy to combine on the same day
Weekend afternoons are busy with families; weekday mornings with school groups
Rooftop high-wire bicycle is a favourite for older kids
places.kids: Kids love pushing every button, the giant soap bubbles and the high-wire bicycle; pair it with the Oceanário next door for a full rainy day.

places.name: Telecabine Lisboa (Parque das Nações cable car)
places.summary: A gondola running along the Tagus riverfront in Parque das Nações, between the Oceanário area and the Vasco da Gama tower. It gives a gentle, short ride with views of the river and the long Vasco da Gama Bridge.
facts: Ride is about 10 minutes each way
One-way or return tickets; buy at either station
Combine with the Oceanário and the riverside gardens
Can stop in strong winds
places.kids: Kids love floating above the riverside in the little cabins; ride one way and walk back along the flat promenade past fountains and playgrounds.

places.name: Parque Recreativo do Alvito (Monsanto)
places.summary: A shaded recreation park inside Monsanto Forest Park, Lisbon's large green lung. It has big playgrounds, picnic tables under the pines and space to cycle and run.
facts: Free entry
Best reached by car or taxi
Popular for weekend family picnics; bring food
Summer pool in the park opens only in the hot months
places.kids: Kids love the big playgrounds and running under the pines; pack a picnic and come on a hot day for the shade.

places.name: Eduardo VII Park & Estufa Fria
places.summary: Lisbon's central hillside park with clipped hedges and views down to the river. On its western side, the Estufa Fria is a shaded greenhouse garden with ponds, fish, ferns and little paths.
facts: The park is free; the Estufa Fria has a small fee
Marquês de Pombal and Parque metro stations are close
Playground in the park
Estufa Fria is a good shady or drizzly-day option
places.kids: Kids love the jungle-like greenhouse with goldfish ponds, tiny bridges and caves; then run down the long park lawns towards the river view.

places.name: Jardim da Estrela
places.summary: A pretty, flat 19th-century garden opposite the Estrela Basilica, loved by local families. It has a good playground, a duck pond, an old bandstand and a kiosk café.
facts: Free entry
Tram 28 stops at the gate
Kiosk café for coffee while kids play
Easy break between sightseeing in central Lisbon
places.kids: Kids love the playground, ducks and carp in the pond; a perfect hour of downtime while parents have a coffee at the kiosk.

places.name: Calouste Gulbenkian Planetarium
places.summary: A domed planetarium in Belém, next to the Jerónimos Monastery and the Navy Museum. It runs star shows for different ages, some aimed at young children.
facts: Check session times and languages in advance
Sessions last about 30–45 minutes
Easy to combine with the Navy Museum next door
places.kids: Kids love lying back under the dome to explore the night sky; choose a children's session and book ahead.

places.name: Navy Museum (Museu de Marinha)
places.summary: Portugal's maritime museum in a wing of the Jerónimos Monastery in Belém. It is packed with model ships, navigation instruments and a hall of real royal barges and seaplanes.
facts: In the west wing of the Jerónimos Monastery
Often far quieter than the monastery itself
The big hall of royal barges and seaplanes is the highlight
Combine with the Planetarium next door
places.kids: Kids love the huge golden royal barges, ship models and early seaplanes; a great rainy-day alternative in Belém.

places.name: Quinta Pedagógica dos Olivais
places.summary: A small city farm run by Lisbon's council in the Olivais district. Children can see farm animals, vegetable gardens and traditional rural crafts close to the airport and Parque das Nações.
facts: Free entry
Small and low-key: ideal for toddlers
Workshops for children on some weekends
Close to the airport: a good stop on arrival or departure day
places.kids: Little ones love the donkeys, goats, rabbits and hens; go in the morning and combine with Parque das Nações.

places.name: Carris Museum (Tram Museum)
places.summary: Lisbon's public-transport museum in the Santo Amaro depot in Alcântara. It displays historic trams and buses in old sheds, and a vintage tram carries visitors between the halls.
facts: In Alcântara, on the tram 15 line to Belém
A historic tram shuttles you between the exhibition halls
Kids can climb aboard several old trams and buses
places.kids: Kids love riding the old tram between the halls and climbing into vintage trams and buses; stop on the way to Belém.

places.name: Vasco da Gama Aquarium
places.summary: A small, historic aquarium in Dafundo (Oeiras), founded in 1898, on the riverside road from Lisbon to Cascais. Besides live tanks it has an old-fashioned collection of preserved sea creatures.
facts: Much smaller and cheaper than the Oceanário
Easy stop on the way to Cascais (Cruz Quebrada train station nearby)
Old-fashioned cabinets of preserved specimens fascinate older kids
places.kids: Kids enjoy the fish tanks and the cabinet-of-curiosities feel; a short, cheap visit on the way to Cascais.

places.name: Tropical Botanical Garden (Belém)
places.summary: A peaceful botanical garden behind the Jerónimos Monastery with exotic trees, ponds and roaming peacocks and ducks. A quiet green break from the busy Belém monuments.
facts: Small entry fee
Entrance near the Jerónimos Monastery and Pastéis de Belém
Flat gravel paths and shade
places.kids: Kids love chasing (gently) the peacocks, geese and ducks around the ponds; a calm break between Belém sights.

places.name: Parque Marechal Carmona
places.summary: Cascais's central park next to the Citadel and museums, with shady paths, a duck pond and free-roaming peacocks and chickens. It has a good playground and a café.
facts: Free entry
A few minutes' walk from Cascais station and the beaches
Combine with the Santa Marta Lighthouse Museum next door
places.kids: Kids love the peacocks, roosters and turtles in the pond and the shady playground; a perfect break after the beach.

places.name: Santa Marta Lighthouse Museum
places.summary: A small museum in a blue-and-white striped lighthouse at the mouth of a little cove in Cascais. It explains how lighthouses work and lets visitors climb to a viewpoint.
facts: Small fee; short visit
Next to Parque Marechal Carmona and the marina
Shows giant lighthouse lenses and lamps
places.kids: Kids love the giant glittering lighthouse lenses and the striped tower; combine with the park next door.

places.name: Quinta do Pisão (Parque de Natureza)
places.summary: A nature park and working farm in the Sintra-Cascais Natural Park near Alcabideche. Families can walk easy trails among fields with donkeys, cows and goats, and see organic vegetable gardens.
facts: Free entry to the park trails
Guided activities and donkey walks on some weekends: check ahead
Wear trainers: trails are dirt tracks
Bring water and sun protection
places.kids: Kids love meeting the donkeys and farm animals on the easy dirt tracks; go in the morning and use an all-terrain buggy.

places.name: Cascais–Estoril seafront promenade (Paredão)
places.summary: A flat seafront promenade of about 3 km linking Cascais and São João do Estoril along small sandy beaches. It is the easiest family walk on the coast, with cafés and ice cream along the way.
facts: Flat and paved all the way
Train stations at both ends for an easy return
Waves can splash over the wall in storms
places.kids: Kids love beach-hopping and watching the trains and waves; walk one way and take the train back.

places.name: Praia do Tamariz & ocean pool
places.summary: A sheltered town beach in Estoril right below the train station, with a seawater swimming pool built into the rocks. Calm water most days makes it a favourite for families.
facts: Next to Estoril train station
The ocean pool (piscina oceânica) is open in summer
Lifeguards in the bathing season
places.season: Ocean pool and lifeguards in summer only.
places.kids: Kids love the calm water and the saltwater pool in the rocks; arrive early in summer to get a spot.

places.name: Praia da Conceição & Praia da Duquesa (Cascais)
places.summary: Two joined, sheltered sandy beaches in central Cascais, right by the station. Gentle water, lifeguards in summer and cafés make them easy with small children.
facts: Walk from Cascais train station
Lifeguards in summer
Sunbeds and umbrellas for rent in season
places.kids: Kids love the gentle waves and digging in the sand; come early or late in summer when it is less crowded.

places.name: Sintra Tram (Elétrico de Sintra)
places.summary: A vintage tram line running from near Sintra town through the countryside to the beach at Praia das Maçãs. The open-sided cars rattle through villages and woods.
facts: Runs on a limited timetable, mostly Friday to Sunday: check before going
About 45 minutes each way
Combine with a beach afternoon at Praia das Maçãs
places.season: Limited timetable, more frequent in summer; may not run on some days.
places.kids: Kids love the bell-ringing vintage tram ride to the seaside; check the timetable and ride it out to the beach for lunch.

places.name: Praia das Maçãs
places.summary: A lively family beach on the Sintra coast at the end of the vintage tram line. A small river meets the sea here, with a seafront of cafés and a summer ocean pool nearby.
facts: End of the Sintra tram line
Lifeguards in summer
Atlantic beach: waves can be big
places.caution: Atlantic waves; swim only when lifeguards are on duty.
places.kids: Kids love the tram ride there and splashing where the stream meets the beach; stay in the shallows and near lifeguards.

places.name: Parque da Liberdade (Sintra)
places.summary: A wooded park on the hillside between Sintra's station and the historic centre. Shady trails, a playground and picnic spots offer a free break from the crowded palaces.
facts: Free entry
On the walk from Sintra station to the centre
Some sloping paths and steps
places.kids: Kids love the playground and wooded paths; a free, shady place to let off steam between palace visits.

places.name: Praia da Figueirinha
places.summary: The closest Arrábida beach to Setúbal, with a long sandbank and very shallow, calm water at low tide. It is one of the easiest beaches in the area for young children.
facts: About 15 minutes' drive from Setúbal
Summer car access and parking are limited; a shuttle bus may run
Very shallow at low tide: great for toddlers
Lifeguards and a beach café in summer
places.kids: Kids love the warm, shallow lagoon-like water at low tide; check the tide times and go early in summer.

places.name: Parque Urbano de Albarquel
places.summary: A riverside park on the western edge of Setúbal with playgrounds, lawns, cycling paths and a small sandy beach on the Sado estuary. Its calm water and shade make it an easy family stop.
facts: Free entry and parking
Flat paved paths along the river
Estuary beach with calm water
places.kids: Kids love the playgrounds and the calm little river beach; bring a picnic and watch the boats going to Tróia.

places.name: Lagoa de Albufeira
places.summary: A large coastal lagoon south of Costa da Caparica, separated from the ocean by a sandbar. Its warm, calm water is ideal for small children and for trying paddle boards or kayaks.
facts: Calm, warm water on the lagoon side
Ocean side has big waves: keep kids on the lagoon
Water-sports schools rent kayaks and SUPs in summer
places.kids: Kids love paddling in the warm, still lagoon; older ones can try a kayak or paddle board.

places.name: Setúbal–Tróia ferry
places.summary: The short ferry across the Sado estuary from Setúbal to the Tróia peninsula. It is a cheap, easy boat trip with a good chance of spotting dolphins.
facts: Crossing takes about 20–25 minutes
Passenger catamaran and car ferry depart from separate terminals
Look out for the Sado dolphins on the way
places.kids: Kids love the ferry ride and looking out for dolphins from the deck; take the passenger catamaran and walk to the Tróia beaches.

places.name: Fort of São Filipe (Setúbal)
places.summary: A 16th-century star-shaped fortress on a hill above Setúbal. Its walls give sweeping views over the city, the Sado estuary and Tróia.
facts: Short drive or steep walk up from the centre
Great sunset views over the estuary
Tiled chapel inside the walls
places.caution: High walls; hold small children's hands near the edges.
places.kids: Kids enjoy exploring the walls of a real fort and spotting ships and dolphins below; go late afternoon for the views.

places.name: Transpraia beach train (Costa da Caparica)
places.summary: A narrow-gauge summer beach train that runs along the dunes of Costa da Caparica to Fonte da Telha, stopping at beach after beach. It is a fun way for families to reach quieter beaches.
facts: Runs in the summer season only
About 9 km of track with many beach stops
Pay on board; ride as far as you like
places.season: Runs only in summer (roughly June–September).
places.kids: Kids love the open little train through the dunes; ride it to a quieter beach further south.

places.name: Parque da Paz (Almada)
places.summary: Almada's big urban park across the river from Lisbon, with a lake, lawns, trails and playgrounds. A local favourite for picnics and cycling.
facts: Free entry
Lake with ducks and wide paths
Easy stop on the way to Costa da Caparica
places.kids: Kids love the ducks on the lake and the playgrounds; a good picnic stop on the way to the beaches.

places.name: Praia da Califórnia (Sesimbra)
places.summary: Sesimbra's main town beach, sheltered by the cliffs of Arrábida so the water is usually calm and clear. Cafés, ice cream and the seafront are right next to the sand.
facts: Right in Sesimbra town
Usually calm water thanks to the sheltered bay
Parking is tight in summer: arrive early
places.kids: Kids love the calm, clear water right by town; combine with the castle and grilled fish for lunch.

places.name: Bacalhôa Buddha Eden
places.summary: A huge oriental garden on a wine estate near Bombarral, with giant golden Buddhas, terracotta warriors, lakes and modern sculptures. Big, open and full of surprises, it is easy and fun to explore with children.
facts: Entry ~€5 per adult, young children free
A little tourist train tours the park for a small fee
Lots of walking: wear comfy shoes and bring hats
~20 min from Óbidos
places.kids: Kids love spotting the giant Buddhas, the rows of terracotta warriors and the koi in the lakes; take the little train if small legs get tired, and bring hats as shade is limited.

places.name: Dino Parque Lourinhã
places.summary: Portugal's largest open-air dinosaur park, with well over a hundred life-size models along forest trails, many based on fossils found in the Lourinhã area. There is a fossil lab, digging zones and play areas, making it a top family day out.
facts: Adults ~€14, children ~€11, under 4 free
Buy tickets online to skip the queue in summer
Trails are mostly earth paths in pine forest
~30 min from Óbidos
places.kids: Kids love the life-size dinosaurs hidden in the pine woods and digging for fossils in the sandpit; arrive at opening time in summer and bring a picnic.

places.name: Nazaré Funicular
places.summary: The historic funicular that climbs the cliff from Nazaré's beach to the Sítio clifftop quarter. A short, steep ride with a great view of the beach and the town.
facts: Runs every few minutes, a few euros per ride
Buggies can go on board
Combine with the Sítio viewpoint and the walk to the lighthouse fort
places.kids: Kids love the steep ride up the cliff and the view over the beach from the top; sit at the lower end of the car for the best view.

places.name: Óbidos Lagoon (Foz do Arelho)
places.summary: A large coastal lagoon separated from the sea by a sandbar at Foz do Arelho. The lagoon side has calm, shallow, warmer water that is ideal for small children, with the ocean beach just across the sand.
facts: Free; parking by the lagoon and the beach
Swim on the lagoon side, not where the lagoon opens to the sea
Popular for kayaking and paddleboarding
~15 min from Óbidos and Caldas da Rainha
places.kids: Kids love paddling in the shallow, calm lagoon water and digging in the sand; stay well away from the channel where the lagoon meets the sea, as the current there is strong.
places.caution: Strong currents at the lagoon mouth and on the ocean side.

places.name: Parque D. Carlos I (Caldas da Rainha)
places.photoSearch: Parque D. Carlos I Caldas da Rainha
places.summary: A romantic 19th-century park in the centre of Caldas da Rainha with a big lake, shady trees, ducks and a playground. A relaxed stop near Óbidos, close to the town's daily fruit market.
facts: Free
Rowing boats on the lake in the warmer months
Combine with the morning fruit market in Praça da Fruta
places.kids: Kids love feeding the ducks, the playground and rowing on the lake; go in the morning together with the colourful fruit market.

places.name: Tapada Nacional de Mafra
places.summary: The walled former royal hunting park of Mafra Palace, with forests where deer, fallow deer and wild boar roam. Families can follow marked walking trails, see birds of prey and take a guided ride through the park.
facts: Entry a few euros per person, cheaper for children
Several marked trails of different lengths
Birds-of-prey demonstrations on some days
~10 min from Mafra Palace
places.kids: Kids love spotting deer and wild boar in the woods and watching the birds of prey; walk quietly on the shorter trail early or late in the day for the best animal sightings.

places.name: Aldeia Típica José Franco (Sobreiro)
places.summary: A whimsical miniature village built by potter José Franco, with tiny houses, mills, workshops and moving figures of traditional rural life. Free to wander and a favourite with small children between Mafra and Ericeira.
facts: Free entry
Traditional bakery selling bread with chouriço
Combine with Mafra Palace or Ericeira, both ~10 min away
places.kids: Kids love the tiny houses, windmills and moving figures they can peek into; follow it with a warm bread roll from the village bakery.

places.name: Leiria Castle
places.summary: A medieval castle on a hill above Leiria, with a keep, a royal palace loggia and wide views over the city. A good, manageable castle to explore with children, with the city's riverside parks below.
facts: Entry a few euros, children cheaper
Steep climb from the old town: park near the top if possible
Riverside park and playgrounds along the Lis below the castle
places.kids: Kids love climbing the keep and looking out from the palace loggia over the city; drive up close to the gate with little ones and go down to the riverside playgrounds afterwards.

places.name: Aljubarrota Battle Interpretation Centre (CIBA)
places.photoSearch: Centro de Interpretação da Batalha de Aljubarrota
places.summary: A modern museum on the actual battlefield of Aljubarrota (1385), with a dramatic multimedia show about the battle that secured Portugal's independence. Children can try on helmets and see the battle traps used by the Portuguese army.
facts: Adults ~€7, children cheaper, family tickets
The multimedia show is the highlight: check the session times
~5 min from Batalha Monastery
places.kids: Kids love the loud multimedia film of the battle and trying on armour; visit right before Batalha Monastery so they know the story behind it.

places.name: Grutas da Moeda
places.summary: A show cave near Fátima with colourful, well-lit chambers full of stalactites and stalagmites, named after the legend of a lost coin. Smaller and shorter than Mira de Aire, it suits younger children well.
facts: Guided tour about 45 minutes
Adults ~€8, children cheaper
Constant cool temperature: bring a layer
~5 min from Fátima
places.kids: Kids love the coloured lights on the stalactites and the shapes the guide points out; carry babies in a sling because of the steps, and bring a jumper.

places.name: Parque do Mouchão (Tomar)
places.summary: A shady island park on the Nabão river in the centre of Tomar, with a large old water wheel, ducks and riverside paths. A calm break after the Convent of Christ.
facts: Free
Next to the old town and the riverside cafés
Easy flat paths
places.kids: Kids love the big turning water wheel and the ducks on the river; bring bread crumbs and let them run around in the shade.

places.name: National Railway Museum (Entroncamento)
places.summary: Portugal's national railway museum in the railway town of Entroncamento, with steam locomotives, royal carriages and historic trains in big old sheds. Train-mad children can get close to dozens of engines.
facts: Adults ~€5, children cheaper
Closed on Mondays
Next to Entroncamento station: reachable by train from Lisbon
~20 min from Tomar
places.kids: Kids love the huge steam engines and the royal train carriages; combine it with a real train ride to Entroncamento to make a day of it.

places.name: Portugal dos Pequenitos
places.summary: A miniature park in Coimbra where children can walk into small-scale versions of Portuguese houses, monuments and buildings from the former colonies. A classic Portuguese family day out, just across the river from the old town.
facts: Adults ~€15, children 3–13 ~€10, under 3 free
Small indoor museums of costumes, furniture and the navy
Easy walk across the Santa Clara bridge from the old town
places.kids: Young kids love walking into the child-sized houses and palaces; go at opening time on weekends to beat the school groups.

places.name: Exploratório – Ciência Viva Coimbra
places.photoSearch: Exploratório Centro Ciência Viva de Coimbra
places.summary: Coimbra's hands-on Ciência Viva science centre in the Parque Verde do Mondego, with interactive exhibits and a planetarium. A great rainy-day option close to Portugal dos Pequenitos.
facts: Adults ~€7, children cheaper, family tickets
Planetarium sessions at set times
Riverside park with paths and playground outside
places.kids: Kids love pushing buttons, experimenting and the planetarium shows; check the session times and follow it with a run along the riverside park.

places.name: Botanical Garden of the University of Coimbra
places.wiki: Botanical Garden of the University of Coimbra
places.summary: An 18th-century botanical garden on terraces below the university, with greenhouses, a bamboo forest and huge old trees. A green escape from the steep old town.
facts: The outdoor garden is free
Terraced with stairs between levels
Bamboo grove and tropical greenhouse are the highlights
places.kids: Kids love getting lost in the bamboo forest and spotting the giant trees; enter from the upper gate near the aqueduct to avoid climbing with a buggy.

places.name: Moliceiro boat trip, Aveiro
places.summary: A short boat ride on Aveiro's canals in a brightly painted moliceiro, the traditional seaweed-collecting boat. It is the classic way for families to see the town.
facts: About 45 minutes, ~€15 adults, children cheaper
Boats leave from the Canal Central all day
Fold the buggy on board
places.kids: Kids love the colourful painted boats and ducking under the low bridges; sit near the front, and finish with a box of ovos moles from the canal-side shops.

places.name: Fábrica – Ciência Viva Aveiro
places.photoSearch: Fábrica Centro Ciência Viva de Aveiro
places.summary: A hands-on science centre run with the University of Aveiro in an old factory building in the town centre. It has interactive exhibits and workshops on science and technology.
facts: Adults ~€4, children cheaper
Workshops at weekends, often in Portuguese
Short walk from the Canal Central
places.kids: Kids love the experiments they can try themselves; a good indoor hour between canal walks on a rainy day.

places.name: Ílhavo Maritime Museum
places.photoSearch: Museu Marítimo de Ílhavo aquário bacalhau
places.summary: A maritime museum about the cod-fishing fleets, with a full-size fishing ship and a large aquarium of live Atlantic cod. Fun for children and close to Costa Nova.
facts: Adults ~€5, children cheaper
The cod aquarium is the highlight: check feeding times
~10 min from Aveiro, ~10 min from Costa Nova
places.kids: Kids love the big cod swimming around the aquarium and climbing on the deck of the fishing ship; ask about feeding times when you arrive.

places.name: São Jacinto Dunes Nature Reserve
places.photoSearch: Reserva Natural das Dunas de São Jacinto
places.summary: A protected dune and pine forest reserve on the sandbar north of Aveiro, with a boardwalk trail, bird hides and wild beaches. Reach it by the short ferry from Forte da Barra for a fun adventure.
facts: Free; the trail is about 7 km, but shorter loops are possible
Ferry from Forte da Barra (Gafanha da Nazaré) to São Jacinto
Bring water and snacks: few services
places.kids: Kids love the ferry crossing and looking for birds from the hides along the boardwalk; do a short loop with younger ones and bring binoculars.

places.name: Parque Biológico da Serra da Lousã
places.photoSearch: Parque Biológico da Serra da Lousã
places.summary: A wildlife park in Miranda do Corvo with native Portuguese animals such as wolves, deer, wild boar, otters and birds of prey, alongside farm animals and a rural museum. A gentle family stop on the way to the Lousã schist villages.
facts: Adults ~€8, children cheaper
Mostly outdoor paths on a gentle slope
~30 min from Coimbra
places.kids: Kids love seeing the wolves, otters and farm animals up close; go in the morning when the animals are most active.

places.name: Senhora da Piedade River Beach & Lousã Castle
places.summary: A small river beach in a wooded valley below Lousã's medieval castle and hilltop chapels. In summer families swim in the clear pool; all year it is a lovely spot to explore the little castle.
facts: Free
Swimming best in July–August
~5 min from Lousã, ~30 min from Talasnal
places.kids: Kids love splashing in the cool river pool and climbing the small castle above it; bring water shoes for the stony bottom.
places.season: River swimming is mainly July–September; outside summer it is a walk and castle visit.
places.photoSearch: Senhora da Piedade River Beach & Lousã Castle

places.name: Loriga River Beach
places.summary: A river beach in a granite glacial valley of Serra da Estrela, with clear mountain water, a lawn and natural pools. One of the prettiest places to cool off in the mountains in summer.
facts: Free
Lifeguards and a café in summer
Water is cold even in August
~30 min from Seia
places.kids: Kids love splashing in the clear, rocky pools and playing on the grass; go in July or August, and bring water shoes and warm towels as the water is cold.
places.season: Best July–August, when lifeguards and the café are open.

places.name: Serra da Estrela Interpretation Centre (CISE)
places.photoSearch: Centro de Interpretação da Serra da Estrela Seia
places.summary: An interactive centre in Seia explaining the geology, glaciers, wildlife and shepherding life of Serra da Estrela. A good introduction before going up the mountain, and a fallback when weather closes the road.
facts: Entry a few euros, children cheaper
Interactive displays and models
Good plan when fog or snow closes the road to Torre
places.kids: Kids enjoy the interactive displays about glaciers and mountain animals; visit before driving up to Torre so they know what to look for.

places.name: SEA LIFE Porto
places.summary: Indoor aquarium by the sea at Castelo do Queijo, with sharks, rays, turtles and a walk-through ocean tunnel. An easy, compact visit that works for every age, rain or shine.
facts: Adults ~€17–20, children ~€13–15, under 3 free; cheaper online
Next to Parque da Cidade and the seafront
Free street parking nearby; bus from the centre
Feeding talks run through the day
places.kids: Kids love the underwater tunnel with sharks overhead and the touch pool; book online and combine with the park next door.

places.name: World of Discoveries
places.summary: Interactive museum and theme park about the Portuguese voyages of discovery, in Miragaia near the river. Kids board replica ships and finish with a boat ride through scenes of the explorers' world.
facts: Adults ~€15–20, children cheaper, family tickets available
Allow 1.5–2 h
10 min walk from Ribeira along the river
Mostly indoors; good rainy-day option
places.kids: Kids love the indoor boat ride past Brazil, Africa and India and steering the replica caravel; go after lunch when school groups have left.

places.name: Parque da Cidade do Porto
places.summary: Porto's biggest park, 83 ha of lakes, meadows and woods running down to the ocean. Ducks, geese, wide paths and playgrounds make it the city's favourite family green space.
facts: Free entry
Parking at the Avenida da Boavista entrance and by the sea
Next to SEA LIFE and the beach at Castelo do Queijo
Good spot for a picnic
places.kids: Kids love feeding the ducks, chasing geese on the lawns and biking on the long flat paths; pair it with SEA LIFE and the beach.

places.name: Crystal Palace Gardens
places.photoSearch: Jardins do Palácio de Cristal Porto
places.summary: Romantic hilltop gardens in the city centre with peacocks, roosters, fountains and terraces looking over the Douro. A shady break between sights, with a playground and free entry.
facts: Free entry
Peacocks roam freely
Great river views from the terraces
10 min walk from the Clérigos area
places.kids: Kids love chasing (gently) the peacocks and roosters and the small playground; the lower terraces have steep paths, so keep the buggy on the main avenue.

places.name: Parque Biológico de Gaia
places.summary: A 35 ha nature park on the Febros river in Avintes, with a 3 km trail past enclosures of native animals and birds, an old farm and watermills. A gentle, green half day close to Porto.
facts: Small entry fee; children cheaper
Trail ~3 km, mostly gravel and boardwalk
Café and picnic areas
Free parking at the entrance
places.kids: Kids love spotting deer, otters, owls and storks along the trail and the farm animals near the end; allow a slow 2–3 hours and bring a picnic.

places.name: Maia Zoo
places.summary: Small municipal zoo in the centre of Maia, north of Porto, with big cats, primates, reptiles and birds, plus a sea lion show. Compact and affordable, ideal for younger children.
facts: Low entry fee compared with big zoos
Sea lion and bird shows at set times
Metro to Maia, then a short walk
Easy to do in 2–3 h
places.kids: Little ones love the sea lion show and the reptile house; check the show times at the gate and plan around them.

places.name: Porto historic tram (line 1)
places.summary: Vintage wooden trams rattle along the Douro from Infante, near Ribeira, to Passeio Alegre at Foz. A fun ride to the seafront for families who'd rather not drive.
facts: Single ticket ~€6–7 adults; children cheaper
Board at Infante (Ribeira) or Passeio Alegre (Foz)
Every 30 min or so; expect queues in summer
Ride to Foz, then walk the seafront promenade
places.kids: Kids love the clanging bell and wooden seats of the old tram; board at Infante early to grab the front seats, and fold the buggy.

places.name: Gaia Cable Car
places.summary: Short gondola ride over the port lodge rooftops in Vila Nova de Gaia, linking the riverside with Jardim do Morro at the top of the Dom Luís bridge. A neat way to skip the steep climb.
facts: One-way ~€7 adults, children cheaper; return tickets available
Ride takes about 5 min
Lower station on the Gaia riverfront
Saves the steep walk up to the bridge top deck
places.kids: Kids love floating over the rooftops with the bridge right in front; ride up rather than down and walk back across the top deck.

places.name: Porto Planetarium – Ciência Viva
places.summary: Science centre and planetarium at the Campo Alegre university campus, with dome shows about stars and planets and a small hands-on exhibition. A good indoor option for curious kids.
facts: Shows at set times; check the schedule and book ahead
Some shows in Portuguese only; ask for English sessions
Small ticket price
Weekend family sessions
places.kids: Kids love lying back under the dome watching the night sky; book a family session in English in advance.

places.name: Vila do Conde replica ship (Nau Quinhentista)
places.summary: Full-size replica of a 16th-century Portuguese carrack moored on the Ave river beside the old customs house in Vila do Conde. Children can climb aboard and see how sailors lived on the voyages to India.
facts: Small fee; combined ticket with the customs house museum
About 30 min north of Porto by car or metro line B
Riverside parking
Combine with the beach at Vila do Conde
places.kids: Kids love climbing between the decks of the old ship and peeking into the cramped crew quarters; go before or after an afternoon at the beach.

places.name: Penha Cable Car (Guimarães)
places.summary: Cable car from the edge of Guimarães up Monte da Penha, a wooded hill with giant granite boulders, a sanctuary, picnic areas and playgrounds. A green half day out of town with a fun ride each way.
facts: Return ~€5–6 adults, children cheaper
Ride takes about 10 min
Runs daily in summer, weekends in winter: check before going
There's also a road to the top
places.season: Runs daily in summer; limited (often weekends only) in winter.
places.kids: Kids love the swinging cabin ride and scrambling among the huge boulders and caves at the top; take a picnic and spend the afternoon.

places.name: Aquamuseu do Rio Minho
places.photoSearch: Aquamuseu do Rio Minho Vila Nova de Cerveira
places.summary: Freshwater aquarium and fishing museum in Vila Nova de Cerveira on the Minho river, with river fish, otters and old fishing boats. Small and calm, it's a good stop on the way to Valença.
facts: Low entry fee
In the riverside park of Vila Nova de Cerveira
About 15 min from Valença
Combine with the riverside playground
places.kids: Kids love watching the otters play and the big river fish in the tanks; time your visit with the otter feeding.

places.name: Gil Eannes hospital ship
places.photoSearch: Navio Gil Eannes Viana do Castelo
places.summary: Former hospital and support ship for the cod-fishing fleet, now a museum moored in Viana do Castelo harbour. Kids explore the bridge, cabins, operating theatre and engine room.
facts: Small entry fee; children cheaper
Moored near the town centre
Many steep ship ladders
Allow 45–60 min
places.kids: Kids love taking the captain's wheel on the bridge and exploring the old operating room and galley; use a carrier, the ladders are steep.

places.name: Ecopista do Rio Minho
places.photoSearch: Ecopista do Rio Minho Valença Monção
places.summary: Flat, paved cycling and walking path on an old railway line along the Minho river between Valença and Monção. Easy for buggies, balance bikes and family cycling, with river views towards Spain.
facts: Free
About 18 km in total; do any short section
Bike rental available in Valença in season
Picnic spots and river beaches along the way
places.kids: Kids love cycling or scooting on the car-free path past fields and river beaches; start at Valença and turn back whenever they tire.

places.name: Parque Temático do Arnado
places.photoSearch: Parque Temático do Arnado Ponte de Lima
places.summary: Riverside themed garden in Ponte de Lima with little gardens from different eras and continents, a maze-like layout and ponds. Free and flat, right across the medieval bridge from the town.
facts: Free entry
Across the old bridge from the town centre
Flat paths
Near the Lima river beach
places.kids: Kids enjoy running through the small themed gardens and spotting ducks and fish in the ponds; walk over the old bridge to get there.

places.name: Caniçada reservoir boats & kayaks
places.summary: The long Caniçada reservoir below Gerês is ringed by forested mountains and calm water, with small boat rentals, kayaks and pedal boats around Rio Caldo. A relaxed way to enjoy the national park with kids.
facts: Boat and kayak rentals mainly in summer
Prices vary by operator; no licence needed for small motorboats
Life jackets provided
Swim spots along the shore
places.season: Rentals operate mainly June–September.
places.kids: Kids love steering a little motorboat or paddling a kayak on the still green water; go in the morning before the wind picks up.
places.caution: Cold, deep water: keep life jackets on all the time.

places.name: Douro Line train (Régua–Pocinho)
places.summary: Regular trains follow the Douro river through the vineyard terraces from Régua to Pinhão, Tua and Pocinho, one of Europe's most scenic rail rides. In summer a historic steam train runs Régua–Tua on Saturdays.
facts: Régua–Pinhão ~25 min, cheap regional tickets; children half price
Sit on the right (river side) heading east
Historic train in summer: book ahead, ~€40+ adults
Trains every 1–2 h; check the CP timetable
places.season: Historic steam train runs on summer weekends only; regular trains run all year.
places.kids: Kids love the river views and tunnels; do the short Régua–Pinhão hop and come back by boat or train.

places.name: Ecopista do Tâmega
places.summary: Flat greenway on the old Tâmega railway line from Amarante up the valley, through woods and past old stations. Easy for buggies and family cycling.
facts: Free
Do a short out-and-back from Amarante
Mostly shaded
Bike-friendly surface
places.kids: Kids love biking or scooting on the car-free track and spotting the old station buildings; turn around after 2–3 km with little ones.

places.name: Bragança Ciência Viva Centre
places.summary: Hands-on science centre beside the Fervença river in Bragança, focused on energy and the environment. Interactive exhibits make it a good indoor stop in this remote region.
facts: Low entry fee, family tickets
Riverside park next door
Walking distance from the town centre
Closed Mondays at many Ciência Viva centres: check
places.kids: Kids love pressing, spinning and testing the interactive exhibits; follow with a play in the riverside park.

places.name: Iberian Mask and Costume Museum
places.photoSearch: Museu Ibérico da Máscara e do Traje Bragança
places.summary: Small museum below the citadel showing the colourful masks and costumes of the winter 'caretos' festivals of Trás-os-Montes and Zamora. Bright, quick and a little spooky in a fun way.
facts: Small entry fee
At the foot of the citadel
Allow 30–45 min
Combine with the citadel visit
places.kids: Kids love the scary-funny devil masks and fringed costumes; ask which festival each one comes from.

places.name: Parque Biológico de Vinhais
places.summary: Wooded park near Vinhais at the edge of Montesinho with enclosures of native and rare-breed animals, from deer and wild boar to local cattle and donkeys. Trails, a picnic area and cabins make it a gentle nature day.
facts: Low entry fee
About 30 min west of Bragança
Trails on gravel and dirt
Bring a picnic; few services nearby
places.kids: Kids love seeing deer, boar and local donkeys and cattle up close; wear trainers for the dirt paths.

places.name: Chaves Roman Baths Museum
places.summary: Well-preserved Roman bath complex discovered under the centre of Chaves, now seen from walkways above the pools. A quick, impressive glimpse of Roman life on a rainy day.
facts: Small entry fee
In the town centre near the castle keep
Allow 30–45 min
Step-free walkways
places.kids: Kids enjoy looking down into the ancient pools from the glass walkways and imagining Roman bathers; then cross the Roman bridge.

places.name: Badoca Safari Park
places.summary: A large safari park near Vila Nova de Santo André with a tractor-pulled safari ride among zebras, giraffes and antelopes. It also has bird shows, lemurs and a primate island, plus a pool and play areas, so it fills a whole family day.
facts: Adults ~€25, children ~€20, under 3 free (approx)
Safari ride and shows run at set times: plan around them
Lots of walking in the sun: hats, water and sunscreen
Free parking at the entrance
places.kids: Kids love the tractor safari among giraffes and zebras and the bird show; arrive at opening and do the safari first, before the heat.
places.season: Seasonal: roughly spring to autumn, with reduced days at the start and end of the season; check dates before going.

places.name: Fluviário de Mora
places.summary: Europe's first big freshwater aquarium, following a river from its mountain spring to the estuary, set in the Gameiro ecological park. Families see otters, fish and reptiles, then picnic or walk by the river.
facts: Adults ~€12, children ~€8, under 3 free (approx)
Otters are the star: watch their feeding
Gameiro park outside has a river beach and picnic area
About 1 hour 15 min from Lisbon or Évora
places.kids: Kids love the playful otters and the huge river fish tanks; time the visit for feeding and then picnic in the park by the river.

places.name: Centro Ciência Viva de Estremoz
places.summary: A hands-on Earth-science centre in a former convent in Estremoz, all about rocks, dinosaurs, fossils and the planet. Interactive exhibits make it a good break between castles and marble towns.
facts: Small entrance fee, family tickets available
Pairs well with Estremoz castle and the Saturday market
Good rainy-day stop in the Alentejo
places.kids: Kids enjoy the dinosaur and fossil displays and the hands-on rock and earthquake exhibits; combine it with the castle keep up the hill.

places.name: Centro Ciência Viva do Lousal
places.summary: A science centre in an old pyrite mining village, with hands-on science rooms and a reconstructed mine gallery. Kids learn how miners worked, then explore the village and the mine lake.
facts: Small entrance fee; mine gallery visit may be guided
Near Grândola, a short detour on the way to the coast
Mix of indoor rooms and outdoor mining heritage
places.kids: Kids love going down into the mine gallery and the hands-on experiments; ask at the desk for the next guided gallery visit.

places.name: Monte Selvagem animal reserve
places.summary: An animal park in the cork-oak countryside near Lavre (Montemor-o-Novo) with zebras, camels, ostriches, lemurs and farm animals along a walking circuit. It is smaller and calmer than a big zoo, good for young children.
facts: Adults ~€14, children ~€10 (approx)
Outdoors with unpaved paths: sturdy shoes
Picnic area on site
Opening days vary by season (often weekends only in low season): check before going
places.kids: Little ones love the zebras, camels and goats on the walking loop; bring a picnic and go in the morning, as there's little shade at midday.

places.name: Jardim Público de Évora
places.summary: Évora's shady public garden just inside the walls, with peacocks, a playground, a kiosk café and the ruins of the old royal palace. A perfect break between the city's monuments.
facts: Free
Next to the Palace of D. Manuel and the Church of São Francisco
Kiosk café for drinks and snacks
places.kids: Kids love chasing the peacocks and the playground; it's the ideal stop after the Chapel of Bones or the Roman temple.

places.name: Praia Fluvial de Monsaraz
places.summary: A river beach on Lake Alqueva just below the hilltop village of Monsaraz, with sand, calm water and lifeguards in summer. A great way to cool off after visiting the castle.
facts: Free; lifeguards in the bathing season
Calm freshwater, no waves
Little natural shade: bring an umbrella
Bar and toilets in summer
places.kids: Kids love the warm, wave-free lake water and sandy shore; go in the late afternoon after Monsaraz castle, when the sun is lower.
places.season: Best June–September, when lifeguards and the bar operate.

places.name: Mina de São Domingos river beach
places.photoSearch: Praia fluvial Mina de São Domingos
places.summary: A popular river beach on the Tapada Grande reservoir next to the abandoned São Domingos copper mine near Mértola. Families combine a swim with a look at the colourful old mine ruins.
facts: Free; lifeguards and café in summer
Calm reservoir water, sandy shore and grass
About 20 min from Mértola
Shady trees near the beach
places.kids: Kids love swimming in the calm reservoir and the grassy shade for picnics; look at the old mine ruins from the road, not up close.
places.season: Best June–September, when lifeguards are on duty.
places.caution: Don't let kids play in the mine area or its acidic, coloured water.

places.name: Praia das Furnas (Milfontes)
places.photoSearch: Praia das Furnas Vila Nova de Milfontes
places.summary: A sandy beach on the south bank of the Mira estuary opposite Vila Nova de Milfontes, with calmer water than the open coast. In summer a small ferry crosses from the town.
facts: Free parking on the south bank; small ferry from Milfontes in summer
Calmer river side is best for small children
Lifeguards in the bathing season
places.kids: Kids love the shallow, sheltered river edge and the little ferry crossing; stay on the estuary side and avoid the river mouth at tide changes.
places.caution: Strong tidal currents near the river mouth.

places.name: Zoomarine
places.summary: A marine theme park in Guia near Albufeira with dolphin, sea lion and bird shows, aquariums, rides, pools and a beach area. It is the Algarve's best-known family day out.
facts: Adults ~€35, children 3–10 ~€25, under 3 free (approx); cheaper online
Check the show timetable on arrival
Bring swimwear for the pools and beach area
Large free car park
places.kids: Kids love the dolphin and sea lion shows and the splash pools; plan the day around show times and bring swimwear.
places.season: Usually open about March to early November; closed in winter.

places.name: Aqualand Algarve
places.summary: A big water park at Alcantarilha with high-speed slides, a lazy river and a children's area. A good hot-day treat for older kids.
facts: Adults ~€30, children ~€22 (approx); online discounts
Height limits apply on big slides
Free parking
places.kids: Older kids love the big slides, while little ones have their own shallow area; arrive at opening to grab a shady spot.
places.season: Summer only, roughly June to mid-September.

places.name: Slide & Splash
places.summary: One of the Algarve's oldest and largest water parks, near Lagoa, with dozens of slides, wave-free pools and a kids' zone. A full day of splashing.
facts: Adults ~€30, children ~€22 (approx)
Height limits apply on big slides
Free parking
places.kids: Kids love the pirate-themed kids' area and the family slides; bring water shoes, as the paths get hot.
places.season: Summer only, roughly June to mid-September.

places.name: Aquashow Park
places.summary: A water park in Quarteira with slides, a wave pool, a roller coaster and a hotel, near Vilamoura. Handy for families staying around Faro or Albufeira.
facts: Adults ~€30, children ~€22 (approx)
Has an indoor water area too
Height limits apply on big slides
places.kids: Kids love the wave pool and the family slides; buy tickets online and go on a weekday for shorter queues.
places.season: Outdoor park opens in summer, roughly June to mid-September.

places.name: Lagos Zoo
places.photoSearch: Lagos Zoo Barão de São João
places.summary: A small, shady zoo near Barão de São João, inland from Lagos, focused on primates, birds and smaller animals, with a children's farm. It's easy to see in a morning with toddlers.
facts: Adults ~€20, children ~€14 (approx)
Children's farm with goats and donkeys
Café and picnic area
About 15 min drive from Lagos
places.kids: Little ones love the monkeys, lemurs and the petting farm; go in the morning and finish with a picnic in the shade.

places.name: Centro Ciência Viva de Lagos
places.summary: A small hands-on science centre in Lagos old town, themed on the Age of Discoveries, navigation and the stars. A good rainy-day hour in town.
facts: Small entrance fee
In the old town, walkable from the marina
Best for primary-school-age kids
places.kids: Kids enjoy the navigation and astronomy experiments; it's a quick indoor break when the beach is off.

places.name: Centro Ciência Viva do Algarve
places.photoSearch: Centro Ciência Viva do Algarve Faro
places.summary: A hands-on science centre by Faro's marina, focused on the sun, the sea and the Ria Formosa lagoon, with a small aquarium. Ideal before or after a boat trip from Faro.
facts: Small entrance fee, family tickets
Next to the marina and boat-trip departures
Good on hot or rainy days
places.kids: Kids love the touch tanks and the light and sound experiments; pair it with a Ria Formosa boat trip from the dock outside.

places.name: Centro Ciência Viva de Tavira
places.summary: A small science centre in Tavira's old town with hands-on exhibits about light, energy and the sun. Easy to slot into a day in Tavira.
facts: Small entrance fee
In the town centre, near the river
Best for ages 5–12
places.kids: Kids enjoy the hands-on light and energy experiments; combine with an ice cream by the Roman bridge.

places.name: Quinta de Marim (Ria Formosa)
places.summary: The Ria Formosa Natural Park centre near Olhão, with an easy nature trail past a tide mill, salt pans and lagoon shores. Families spot birds, crabs and, with luck, chameleons.
facts: Small entrance fee
Flat trail of about 3 km, mostly unpaved
Bring binoculars, water and hats
Close to Olhão market
places.kids: Kids love spotting crabs, flamingos and the old tide mill on the flat trail; go early or late in the day for birds and cooler air.

places.name: Dolphin watching from Lagos
places.summary: Boat trips from Lagos marina head out to sea to find common and bottlenose dolphins, often with marine-biologist guides. Many operators run them year-round, weather permitting.
facts: Adults ~€45, children ~€30 (approx); book a day ahead
Trips last about 1.5–2.5 hours
Choose a boat with a cabin or shade for small kids
Morning seas are usually calmer
places.kids: Kids are thrilled when dolphins ride the bow wave; pick a calm morning, bring motion-sickness remedies and leave the buggy in the car.
places.caution: Fast RIB boats can be bumpy and some operators set minimum ages; check before booking.

places.name: Praia do Barril
places.summary: A long, gentle beach on Ilha de Tavira reached by a little train across the lagoon from Pedras d'El Rei. Next to the beach, the 'anchor cemetery' of old tuna-fishing anchors is fun to explore.
facts: Mini train costs a couple of euros each way; or walk the 1 km path
Lifeguards and cafés in summer
Free parking at Pedras d'El Rei
places.kids: Kids love the little train ride and climbing among the rows of rusty anchors; walk back along the path at the end of the day to see crabs in the lagoon.

places.name: Praia da Rocha
places.summary: Portimão's famous wide beach of golden sand below ochre cliffs, with a long boardwalk, lifeguards and cafés. Lots of space makes it easy with small children.
facts: Free; paid parking along the clifftop
Boardwalk across the sand, good for buggies
Lifeguards in the bathing season
Fortaleza de Santa Catarina at the east end
places.kids: Kids love the huge sandy space and the rock stacks to explore; use the boardwalk with a buggy and set up near a lifeguard post.

places.name: Madeira Aquarium (Porto Moniz)
places.summary: A small aquarium inside the old Fort of São João Baptista in Porto Moniz, showing fish, rays and moray eels from Madeira's own coast. It is a good rainy-day partner to the natural pools next door.
facts: Adults ~€8, children ~€5 (approx)
Allow about an hour; combine with the Porto Moniz natural pools
Parking along the seafront
places.kids: Kids love the big tank of local fish, rays and moray eels in an old fort; pair it with a swim in the natural pools next door.

places.name: São Vicente Caves & Volcanism Centre
places.summary: Guided walks through lava tubes formed by an eruption about 890,000 years ago, followed by a volcanism centre with films and a simulated eruption. It is one of the best indoor options in Madeira.
facts: Combined caves and volcanism centre ticket: adults ~€10, children ~€7 (approx)
Guided tours run every 30 minutes or so and take about 30 minutes
Path is level and lit, but there are a few steps
Free parking
places.kids: Kids love walking through real lava tunnels and the simulated volcano eruption afterwards; bring a light jacket, as it is cool and damp inside.

places.name: Santa Catarina Park
places.summary: A big hillside park in central Funchal with a lake, ducks and swans, lawns and views over the harbour. It has a children's playground and is an easy break between sights.
facts: Free
Next to the marina and the cruise terminal, 10 minutes' walk from the old town
Shaded benches and a café kiosk
places.kids: Kids love the playground, the lake with swans and ducks, and watching cruise ships in the harbour below; good for letting little ones run around after the old town.

places.name: Levada dos Balcões (Ribeiro Frio)
places.summary: The easiest levada walk in Madeira: about 1.5 km each way along a nearly flat water channel through laurel forest to a balcony viewpoint over the central peaks. At the start, Ribeiro Frio has a small trout farm.
facts: Free; about 3 km return, 1–1.5 hours with kids
Paid parking at Ribeiro Frio on the ER103, often full by late morning
Chaffinches come to eat from your hand at the viewpoint
See the trout tanks at the start
places.kids: Kids love the tame chaffinches at the viewpoint and the trout tanks at the start; the path is wide and almost flat, so even small walkers manage it.

places.name: Praia Formosa
places.summary: Funchal's biggest public beach, a long stretch of dark sand and pebbles with lifeguards in summer. A flat seaside promenade leads from here to Câmara de Lobos.
facts: Free; parking and bus from central Funchal
Lifeguards in season, beach cafés and showers
Water shoes help on the pebbles
places.kids: Kids love throwing pebbles and paddling, and the flat promenade is great for scooters; wear water shoes and swim only on calm days.
places.caution: Open Atlantic beach with a quick drop-off; watch children closely in the waves.
places.facilities: Toilets, showers, cafés, lifeguards in season

places.name: Calheta Beach
places.summary: A man-made golden-sand beach protected by breakwaters, so the water is calm and shallow. With the marina and cafés behind it, it is one of the best spots for young children on the main island.
facts: Free; parking by the marina
Sheltered, calm water inside the breakwaters
Cafés, toilets and showers
places.kids: Kids love building sandcastles with golden sand and paddling in the calm water behind the breakwaters; arrive early in summer for space.

places.name: Machico Beach
places.summary: A sheltered golden-sand beach in the bay of Machico, near the airport. Calm water and a seafront promenade with cafés make it an easy family stop on the east side.
facts: Free; parking in town
Sheltered bay, usually calm
Only about 10 minutes from the airport
places.kids: Kids love the soft golden sand and calm water; a good first or last swim near the airport.

places.name: CR7 Museum
places.summary: A small museum on the Funchal seafront showing Cristiano Ronaldo's trophies, boots and shirts. Football-mad kids will love it; others may be done in 20 minutes.
facts: Adults ~€5, children cheaper (approx)
Small; 30–45 minutes is enough
Take a photo with the Ronaldo statue outside
places.kids: Football fans love the hundreds of trophies and the photo with the Ronaldo statue outside; quick and good on a rainy hour.

places.name: Lido pools (Funchal)
places.summary: A seaside swimming complex in Funchal's hotel zone with saltwater pools, a children's pool, sunbeds and sea access by ladders. It is an easy, safe swim day in the city.
facts: Entry a few euros per person (approx), sunbeds extra
Children's pool and lifeguards
Café and changing rooms
places.kids: Kids love the shallow children's pool and the big seaside pool; go in the morning to get sunbeds in summer.
places.season: Open roughly May to October.

places.name: Expolab Ciência Viva (Lagoa)
places.summary: The Ciência Viva hands-on science centre on São Miguel, in Lagoa a short drive from Ponta Delgada. Interactive exhibits on physics, volcanoes and the sea make it the island's best rainy-day option.
facts: Adults ~€5, children cheaper (approx)
Hands-on exhibits, workshops in school holidays
Free parking
places.kids: Kids love pressing every button on the hands-on experiments; perfect when it rains, which it often does in the Azores.

places.name: Gruta do Carvão
places.summary: The longest lava tube on São Miguel, right in Ponta Delgada, with guided tours through part of it. It shows lava stalactites and layered walls from old eruptions.
facts: Guided tours only; book ahead in summer
Adults ~€6–8, children cheaper (approx)
Wear closed shoes; floor is uneven
places.kids: Kids love the dark lava tunnel and the lava 'stalactites' lit up by the guide; wear good shoes and bring a jacket.

places.name: Vila Franca do Campo Islet
places.photoSearch: Ilhéu de Vila Franca do Campo
places.summary: A sunken volcanic crater just off the coast, with a round natural lagoon inside, reached by a short boat from Vila Franca do Campo marina. The calm, clear water inside the ring is great for swimming and snorkelling.
facts: Boat about 15 minutes; return ticket ~€10 adults, less for children (approx)
Visitor numbers are limited in summer: buy tickets early in the day
No shade or shops on the islet: bring water, food and sun shade
places.kids: Kids love the short boat ride and swimming in the calm lagoon inside a volcano crater; bring snorkels, shade and snacks, as there is nothing on the islet.
places.season: Boats run in summer only, roughly June to September.

places.name: António Borges Garden
places.summary: A 19th-century romantic garden in Ponta Delgada with huge trees, ponds, a fake grotto and little tunnels and bridges. Free and central, it is a fun hour of exploring.
facts: Free
Central Ponta Delgada, walking distance from the old town
Some steps around the grottoes
places.kids: Kids love the secret tunnels, grottoes and little bridges among giant trees; a free, easy hour in town.

places.name: Pinhal da Paz forest park
places.summary: A large forest park in the hills above Ponta Delgada with walking paths, gardens, picnic tables with grills and children's play areas. Locals come here for weekend picnics.
facts: Free
Picnic tables and barbecue spots
Toilets and play areas
Bring a jacket; it is cooler than the coast
places.kids: Kids love the playgrounds and forest paths among camellias and cedars; bring a picnic and use the grills like the local families.

places.name: Ribeira dos Caldeirões Natural Park
places.summary: A small, lush park in the northeast of São Miguel with a big waterfall right by the road, old restored watermills and flower-lined paths. Short and easy, it is a good stop on the coast road.
facts: Free, parking on site
Main waterfall is a few minutes' walk from the car park
Small café in season
places.kids: Kids love the tall waterfall right next to the path and peeking into the old watermills; it's short, so good for little legs.

places.name: Arruda Pineapple Plantation
places.photoSearch: Plantação de ananás Arruda Fajã de Baixo
places.summary: A family-run plantation on the edge of Ponta Delgada where Azorean pineapples grow in old whitewashed greenhouses. Visitors can walk through and see the plants at every stage.
facts: Free entry
Takes 30–45 minutes
