Shop with pineapple liqueur, jam and fresh fruit
places.kids: Kids love finding pineapples at every size in the warm greenhouses; a short, free visit, nice on a drizzly day.

places.name: Gruta das Torres
places.summary: The largest lava tube in Portugal, on Pico island, explored on a guided tour with helmets and torches. The tunnel shows lava stalactites and ropy lava floors.
facts: Guided tours only, small groups: book ahead
Adults ~€8, children cheaper (approx)
Helmets and torches provided; wear closed shoes
Minimum age applies (around 6)
places.kids: Kids love wearing a helmet and torch to explore a real lava tube; book ahead and bring a warm layer.
places.caution: Uneven, wet rocky floor; younger children are not allowed on the tour.

places.name: Whalers' Museum (Lajes do Pico)
places.photoSearch: Museu dos Baleeiros Lajes do Pico
places.summary: A museum in old boathouses showing the open whaling boats, harpoons and scrimshaw of Pico's whalers. Lajes is also a top place for whale-watching trips.
facts: Adults ~€2–3, children free or reduced (approx)
Combine with a whale-watching trip from Lajes
About an hour
places.kids: Kids love the real whaling boats and carved whale teeth; combine it with a whale-watching trip from the same harbour.

places.name: Gruta do Natal
places.summary: A lava tube in the centre of Terceira that visitors walk through with a guide or on a lit path, seeing different lava formations. It sits near the Algar do Carvão and Lagoa do Negro.
facts: Combined ticket with Algar do Carvão available (approx €10–15 adults)
Low ceilings in places; wear closed shoes
Seasonal hours, shorter in winter
places.kids: Kids love ducking under the low lava ceilings and spotting shapes in the rock; combine it with Algar do Carvão nearby on a combined ticket.

places.name: Praia da Vitória beach
places.summary: A long sandy beach in a sheltered bay with a marina and seafront promenade on Terceira. It is one of the calmest and sandiest beaches in the Azores, with lifeguards in summer.
facts: Free; parking along the bay
Lifeguards in summer; cafés on the promenade
Close to Lajes airport
places.kids: Kids love the rare soft sand and calm, shallow water in the sheltered bay; the promenade is good for scooters and ice cream.

places.name: Porto Pim beach
places.summary: A small sandy beach in a sheltered bay just south of Horta's centre, with calm water and the old whale factory museum at one end. A short path leads up Monte da Guia for views.
facts: Free; walkable from Horta
Sheltered bay, usually calm
Old whaling factory museum at the end of the bay
places.kids: Kids love the calm, clear water and the soft sand in a small bay right in town; visit the whale factory museum at the end of the beach on a rainy hour.

places.name: Faro Airport (FAO)
places.summary: The Algarve's international airport, just west of Faro.
facts: Car hire desks and shuttle lots
Bus and taxi to Faro ~15 min
Allow extra time in summer

places.name: Madeira Airport (FNC)
places.summary: Madeira's main airport (Cristiano Ronaldo Airport) at Santa Cruz, on a runway partly built on pillars over the sea. About 25 minutes from Funchal.
facts: Aerobus / SAM buses and taxis to Funchal (~€30–35 by taxi)
Strong crosswinds sometimes cause diversions or delays
Car hire desks in arrivals

places.name: Ponta Delgada Airport (PDL)
places.summary: São Miguel's main airport, a few minutes west of Ponta Delgada. Hub for SATA/Azores Airlines inter-island and mainland flights.
facts: Taxi to the centre ~€10
Car hire desks in arrivals — book ahead
Inter-island flights by SATA Air Açores

places.name: Terceira Lajes Airport (TER)
places.summary: Shared civil-military airport on Terceira's north-east coast, about 25 minutes from Angra do Heroísmo.
facts: Taxi to Angra ~€25
Car hire in arrivals
Bus to Angra and Praia da Vitória

places.name: Horta Airport (HOR)
places.summary: Faial's small airport at Castelo Branco, about 10 km west of Horta.
facts: Taxi to Horta ~€12–15
Limited car hire — book ahead
Ferries to Pico leave from Horta harbour

places.name: Lisbon Airport (LIS)
places.summary: Humberto Delgado airport, inside the city: 20–30 min to the centre by metro (red line) or taxi.
facts: Metro red line to the centre; change at Alameda or São Sebastião
Car rental desks in the P2 car park area
Allow 2 h before international flights in summer

places.name: Porto Airport (OPO)
places.summary: Francisco Sá Carneiro airport, ~25 min from central Porto by metro (line E, violet) or car.
facts: Metro line E to Trindade in ~30 min
Tolls: the A28/A4 near Porto are electronic-only in places

checklist: ID for every child: EU children need their own ID card or passport, even babies.
A child travelling with only one parent, or with grandparents: carry a signed consent letter from the other parent(s).
Car seats: children under 135 cm must ride in a child seat in Portugal. Book them with the rental car, or bring your own.
European Health Insurance Card (EU) for each child, or travel insurance. SNS 24 (808 24 24 24) gives health advice by phone.
Sun: hats, high-factor sunscreen and water, even in spring and autumn. Avoid the beach between 12:00 and 16:00 in summer.
Atlantic beaches: strong currents and big waves. Swim only at beaches with lifeguards and a green flag; river beaches and the Algarve's sheltered coves are calmer.
Cliffs (Algarve, Cabo da Roca, Nazaré): hold hands near the edge; many viewpoints have no railing.
Old towns are hilly and cobbled: a sturdy buggy, or a baby carrier, works better than a light city stroller.
Book ahead in summer and school holidays: Oceanário, Zoomarine, dolphin and boat trips, water parks.
Many museums and monuments close on Mondays. Kids under 12 often go free, or pay a reduced price; ask for a family ticket.
Restaurants welcome children; dinner starts late (from 19:30). Most have high chairs; a "meia dose" (half portion) suits kids.
Summer and early autumn: forest fire risk. Follow road closures and keep away from smoke.
